editorial:
Imagine you are stepping back into the sixties to see how the government kept an eye on the money. You follow a Treasury inspector who travels to different towns to catch banks off guard with surprise audits. It feels more like a fly-on-the-wall experience than a dry lecture, giving you a peek at the tension between the government and small-town bankers. Since a young Brian De Palma directed this, you get a sense of curiosity and a steady flow that keeps you interested in the process of these inspections.

What really stands out is how it turns a boring job into a bit of a game, showing the stress on the faces of the bank staff. While it is a documentary, the pacing is surprisingly snappy for its time. It is a great pick for anyone who likes history or wants to see an early project from a famous director.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the final results of the surprise inspections. You see which banks passed the test and which ones were sloppy with their records. The inspector gives a final report that connects the health of a town to the strength of its bank. It ends on a serious note, reminding you that the economy depends on honesty and strict rules to keep everyone's money safe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves early Brian De Palma or government history.
